items.title: Finite reversible Cheeger inequality

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: Theorem 2.5, PDF p. 10; finite reversible-chain conductance bound.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 33, PDF pp. 171–176; history-path spectral-gap comparison.

items.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with $|\Omega|\ge2$. Let $P=(P(x,y))_{x,y\in\Omega}$ be an irreducible row-stochastic matrix and let $\pi$ be a strictly positive stationary probability satisfying detailed balance
$$\pi(x)P(x,y)=\pi(y)P(y,x).$$
For $S\subseteq\Omega$, put $Q(S,S^c)=\sum_{x\in S,\,y\notin S}\pi(x)P(x,y)$, and define the conductance
$$\phi=\min_{0<\pi(S)\le1/2}\frac{Q(S,S^c)}{\pi(S)}.$$
If $1=\lambda_1>\lambda_2\ge\cdots$ are the eigenvalues of $P$ in the weighted inner product $\langle f,g\rangle_\pi=\sum_x\pi(x)f(x)\overline{g(x)}$, then the algebraic gap satisfies
$$1-\lambda_2\ge\frac{\phi^2}{2}.$$
No absolute-gap or aperiodicity assertion is made.
proof_obligations: Give the complete coarea/Cauchy–Schwarz proof and state the reversible transition and conductance conventions.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite sums and finite-dimensional spectral theory only.

items.title: Large clock-penalty perturbation

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: Lemma 3.17, PDF pp. 18–19; clock-penalty gap transfer.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 33, PDF pp. 174–176; local clock penalties and legal subspace.

items.statement:
Let $\mathcal H=S\oplus S^\perp$ be finite-dimensional, let $H_1=H_1^*$ with $\|H_1\|\le K$, and let $H_2=H_2^*\ge0$ satisfy $H_2|_S=0$ and $H_2|_{S^\perp}\ge I$. For $J>2K$, set $H_J=H_1+JH_2$, and let $\mu_1\le\mu_2\le\cdots$ be the eigenvalues of the compression $A=P_SH_1|_S$, where $\dim S\ge2$. With $\epsilon_J=K^2/(J-2K)$, the two smallest eigenvalues of $H_J$ obey
$$\mu_k-\epsilon_J\le\lambda_k(H_J)\le\mu_k\quad(k=1,2).$$
Consequently $\lambda_2(H_J)-\lambda_1(H_J)\ge(\mu_2-\mu_1)-\epsilon_J$; positivity of this bound requires the separate condition $\epsilon_J<\mu_2-\mu_1$. Every unit eigenvector $x=s+t$ of $H_J$ with eigenvalue $\lambda\le K$ also satisfies $\|t\|\le K\|s\|/(J-2K)$. Thus $J>2K$ alone supplies no general gap conclusion.
proof_obligations: Use the variational upper bound and write unit vectors as components in S and S^⊥. Complete the square using the penalty J and cross term ≤2K||v_S||||v_perp||. For gap transfer use min–max for the first two eigenvalues and record the additive error separately. Avoid double-counting J: H₂≥I, not ≥J before multiplication.
items.axiom_use: None; only finite-dimensional spectral and block-matrix arguments are used.

items.title: Partial trace contracts trace distance

references.title: John Watrous, The Theory of Quantum Information, §3.1.1
John Preskill, Quantum Computation, Chapter 2: Foundations I: States and Ensembles

items.statement:
Let $H_A,H_B$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho,\sigma$ be density operators on $H_A\otimes H_B$. Then
$$D(\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho,\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\sigma)\le D(\rho,\sigma).$$
proof_obligations: Step 1.1: Put $X=\rho-\sigma$ and $Y=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}X$. Both are Hermitian. For $Y$, this follows directly from [F1]: conjugating its $(i,i')$ entry and using $X_{(i,j),(i',j)}=\overline{X_{(i',j),(i,j)}}$ gives $\overline{Y_{ii'}}=Y_{i'i}$. By [F2], the two partial traces of $\rho,\sigma$ are density operators, so their trace distance is defined.

Step 1.2: For any finite-dimensional Hermitian $Z$, diagonalize it in an orthonormal basis with eigenvalues $\lambda_i\in\mathbb R$. If $A=A^*$ and $\|A\|\le1$, then each diagonal entry $\langle Ae_i,e_i\rangle$ is real and lies in $[-1,1]$. Hence $|\operatorname{tr}(ZA)|=|\sum_i\lambda_i\langle Ae_i,e_i\rangle|\le\sum_i|\lambda_i|=\|Z\|_1$ by [F3]–[F4]. Equality is a

Step 2.1: For every self-adjoint contraction $A$ on $H_A$, [F5] shows $A\otimes I_{H_B}$ is self-adjoint with norm at most one: its eigenvalues in the product basis are the eigenvalues of $A$, repeated, and each has modulus at most $1$. The pairing identity [F1] gives $\operatorname{tr}(YA)=\operatorname{tr}(X(A\otimes I_{H_B}))$, whose absolute value is at most $\|X\

Step 3.1: Apply the trace-distance definition [F3] to $X=\rho-\sigma$ and $Y=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho-\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\sigma=\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}X$. Step 2.1 gives $2D(\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\rho,\operatorname{Tr}_{H_B}\sigma)=\|Y\|_1\le\|X\|_1=2D(\rho,\sigma)$; division by $2$ proves the assertion.
items.axiom_use: None; only finite-dimensional spectral theory and finite trace sums are used.

items.title: Finite adiabatic path model

references.title: Sabine Jansen, Mary-Beth Ruskai, and Ruedi Seiler, Bounds for the adiabatic approximation with applications to quantum computation
references.locator: Theorems 1 and 3, PDF pp. 3–11; finite-dimensional uniformly gapped spectral bands.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 30, printed pp. 151–156; PDF pp. 159–164.

items.statement:
Let $V$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with inner product linear in its first argument. A **finite adiabatic path** is a family $H(s):V\to V$ of linear endomorphisms ([[def-linear-map]]) indexed by $s\in[0,1]$, whose matrix entries are twice continuously differentiable in $s$ and such that $H(s)=H(s)^*$ for every $s\in[0,1]$. A **coherently followed spectral band** is a norm-continuous family of orthogonal projections $P(s):V\to V$ indexed by $s\in[0,1]$, of one fixed rank $m\ge1$, commuting with $H(s)$, whose range is a sum of full eigenspaces and which locally continues the same isolated cluster. For a finite union of positively oriented circles $\Gamma$, define $\oint_\Gamma F(z)\,dz$ as the sum of the parameterized integrals $\int_0^{2\pi}F(c+re^{it})ire^{it}\,dt$ over its circle components. Local continuation means that on each neighborhood there is such a contour enclosing exactly the selected cluster and
$$P(s)=-\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma(H(s)-zI)^{-1}\,dz.$$
With $Q(s)=I-P(s)$, define the **full gap**
$$g(s)=\min\{|\lambda-\mu|:\lambda\in\sigma(H(s)|_{\operatorname{ran}P(s)}),\ \mu\in\sigma(H(s)|_{\operatorname{ran}Q(s)})\}.$$
If $Q(s)=0$, the full gap is $+\infty$. Admissible gapped paths have a uniform full gap $\inf_{s\in[0,1]}g(s)>0$. Distinct eigenvalues inside the band may cross; its total rank remains $m$.

For a real parameter $T\in\mathbb R$, the slow-time propagator $U_T$ is the unique solution of
$$i\frac{d}{ds}U_T(s)=T H(s)U_T(s),\qquad U_T(0)=I.$$
Identifying complex coordinates with real and imaginary parts reduces this to a real finite matrix ODE ([[lem-linear-matrix-odes-have-unique-global-solutions-on-a-given-interval]]); differentiating $U_T(s)^*U_T(s)$ shows it stays unitary.

An instance also supplies an explicit preparation isometry $A_0:\mathbb C^m\to V$ with image $\operatorname{ran}P(0)$ and its declared preparation cost. For a rank-one band this means a specified unit vector $\psi_0\in\operatorname{ran}P(0)$ and a circuit preparing it; for a rank-$m$ band it is an orthonormal frame, not just the matrix $H(0)$ or the projector $P(0)$. Given an input density operator $\rho_{\rm in}$ on $\mathbb C^m$, the evolved output is $\rho_T=U_T(1)A_0\rho_{\rm in}A_0^*U_T(1)^*$. This is a density operator: for $W=U_T(1)A_0$, $W^*W=A_0^*U_T(1)^*U_T(1)A_0=I$ by isometry and unitarity; hence $W\rho_{\rm in}W^*$ is nonnegative by its quadratic form, and $\operatorname{tr}(W\rho_{\rm in}W^*)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\rm in}W^*W)=1$ by trace cyclicity ([[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]], [[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]], [[thm-trace-of-ab-equals-trace-of-ba]]). A rank-one input is the pure-state projector ([[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]], [[def-qc-density-operator]]). A supplied target density operator $\sigma$ on $V$ is compared with $\rho_T$ by trace distance $D(\rho_T,\sigma)$ ([[def-qc-trace-distance]]). A finite output POVM on $V$ and an accepting outcome set may be supplied; its success probability is the sum of the corresponding POVM probabilities ([[def-qc-povm-and-outcome-law]], [[thm-qc-povm-probabilities-normalize]]). A rank-one output may equivalently be described by a projective measurement on $V$ ([[def-qc-projective-measurement]], [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]]). The model is mathematical and includes no physical postulate.
proof_obligations: Separate model data from the adiabatic theorem; state whether the band is unique ground or rank-m.
If initial amplitudes are supplied as a table, pad the finite basis to a power of two with zero amplitudes and charge table construction, storage, precision and access.
Keep A₀ and C_init as explicit instance data; do not infer an amplitude table, QRAM, or preparation circuit from H(0) or its spectral projector.
items.axiom_use: None; finite-dimensional spectral theory and the finite matrix ODE result use no choice principle.

items.statement: For a $C^2$ finite-dimensional Hermitian path with a coherently followed spectral cluster separated from the complementary spectrum by a positive gap, the spectral projection $P(s)$ is $C^2$ on $[0,1]$.

items.title: Adiabatic path access and resource model

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapters 27–30, printed pp. 133–156; PDF pp. 141–164.

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: §§2–3.1, PDF pp. 7–20; finite path model, local clock access, and circuit conversion.

items.statement:
An **adiabatic path access instance** consists of a finite path model ([[def-qa-36-finite-adiabatic-path-model]]), its exact initial preparation circuit $A_0$ and cost $C_{\rm init}$, a finite term count $r$, and a uniform description
$$H(s)=\sum_{j=1}^r c_j(s)H_j,$$
where the $H_j$ are stated finite-dimensional self-adjoint operators and the real coefficient functions $c_j$ have explicit rational binary inputs, uniform evaluation procedures, certified value errors and certified first-derivative bound $M_1\ge\sup_s\|H'(s)\|$. The access declaration provides, for every allowed time code $u$, either the exact term operation $e^{-iuH_j}$ as a named oracle with its query charge, or a full-list uniform circuit family $V_j(u)$ with a certified bound $\|V_j(u)-e^{-iuH_j}\|\le\eta_j(u)$. Each inverse or controlled call is available only when separately declared. This is the finite term-list access interface of [[def-qa-20-simulation-error-and-cost-model]] and [[def-qa-20-term-list-access-model]].

The resource record lists separately: $C_{\rm init}$; the term count $r$; all term-oracle queries; controlled and inverse calls; gate, clean-ancilla and dirty-ancilla counts; coefficient-precision bits; full circuit-description bits; uniform generator time; and the continuous evolution time $T$. If a physical energy-normalized action is used, it also records $T\sup_s\|H(s)\|$. A missing coordinate is unavailable, not zero. No arbitrary matrix description or spectral projector supplies an initial preparation, term exponential, controlled call, inverse, coefficient evaluator, or circuit generator for free.
proof_obligations: Require uniform polynomial-time evaluation of sampled terms; arbitrary real matrix families are not circuit inputs.

items.title: Finite spectral-band derivative estimates for adiabatic paths

references.title: Sabine Jansen, Mary-Beth Ruskai, and Ruedi Seiler, Bounds for the adiabatic approximation with applications to quantum computation
references.locator: Lemmas 2, 5–8, PDF pp. 6–12; reduced resolvent, twiddle, and derivative bounds.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 30, printed pp. 152–155; finite-dimensional adiabatic projector derivatives.

items.title: Finite JRS adiabatic projector bound

references.title: Sabine Jansen, Mary-Beth Ruskai, and Ruedi Seiler, Bounds for the adiabatic approximation with applications to quantum computation
references.locator: Theorem 3 and Lemmas 1–8, PDF pp. 5–12; endpoint and gap constants.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 30, printed pp. 151–156; PDF pp. 159–164.

items.statement:
Let $H:[0,1]\to\mathcal L(V)$ be a $C^2$ finite-dimensional Hermitian path, and let $P(s)$ be a coherently followed spectral projection of constant rank $m\ge1$, separated from its complement by full gap $g(s)>0$. Let $U_T$ solve $iU_T'(s)=TH(s)U_T(s)$ with $U_T(0)=I$, where $T>0$. Define
$$A_m(s)=\frac1T\left[\frac{m\|H'(0)\|}{g(0)^2}+\frac{m\|H'(s)\|}{g(s)^2}+\int_0^s\left(\frac{m\|H''(r)\|}{g(r)^2}+\frac{7m\sqrt m\|H'(r)\|^2}{g(r)^3}\right)dr\right].$$
Then
$$\|U_T(s)P(0)U_T(s)^*-P(s)\|\le A_m(s).$$
For every unit $\psi\in\operatorname{ran}P(0)$, its transition probability out of the band at time $s$ is at most $A_m(s)^2$. The rank $m$ may be larger than the number of distinct eigenvalues in the band; using rank in the constants is a valid upper bound.
proof_obligations: Specialize JRS Theorem 3 to finite dimension; retain C² regularity, constant rank, coherent isolated projection, full gap, endpoint terms and all constants/gap powers.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite-dimensional spectral and matrix ODE results only.

items.title: Five-local history-state adiabatic path

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: §§3.1.1–3.1.3, PDF pp. 10–15; five-local unary-clock construction and history-state padding.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 33, printed pp. 171–176; history-state construction, unary clock, and adiabatic path.

items.statement:
**Input:** A full-list uniform circuit on $n\ge1$ qubits with $L\ge1$ listed gates $U_1,\ldots,U_L$, each acting on at most two data qubits, and a rational tolerance $0<\varepsilon\le1$. Circuit products act right to left ([[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]]). The computation is applied to the explicitly supplied all-zero input preparation $A_0$; its wire and preparation cost $C_{\rm init}$ is recorded by [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]] and [[def-qa-36-adiabatic-resource-model]]. The path-access input also supplies uniform term-time providers for the constructed term list, exact coefficient evaluation, supported time codes and certified call errors required by [[alg-qa-36-discretized-path-simulation]].

**Output:** The explicit finite term list and linearly interpolated Hamiltonian path $H(s)$, together with the supplied initial preparation and resource coordinates, plus the evolution access schedule and data-register output produced by steps 5–7 when the required access providers are available. The schedule uses the declared circuit-family or named-oracle provider for each term call and records its corresponding resource charge.

1. Set $K=\lceil2L/\varepsilon\rceil$ and $N=L+K$. Append $K$ identity gates, writing $U_\ell=I$ for $L<\ell\le N$. Use data space $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$ and an ordered $N$-qubit clock register ([[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]], [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]). Its legal unary clock basis is
$$|c_\ell\rangle=|1^\ell0^{N-\ell}\rangle,\qquad0\le\ell\le N.$$

2. Let $H_{\rm clock}=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}|01\rangle\langle01|_{{\rm clock}_j,{\rm clock}_{j+1}}$ and
$$H_{\rm input}=\sum_{i=1}^n |1\rangle\langle1|_{{\rm data}_i}\otimes|0\rangle\langle0|_{{\rm clock}_1},\qquad H_{\rm clock0}=\sum_{j=1}^N|1\rangle\langle1|_{{\rm clock}_j}.$$
The first tensor factor is the data register. The zero-summand convention applies when an index range is empty.

3. For each transition $\ell-1\to\ell$, specify two local clock patterns $a_\ell,b_\ell$: if $1<\ell<N$, use $a_\ell=100,b_\ell=110$ on clock bits $(\ell-1,\ell,\ell+1)$; for $\ell=1$, use $a_1=00,b_1=10$ on bits $(1,2)$; for $\ell=N$, use $a_N=10,b_N=11$ on bits $(N-1,N)$. For a clock pattern $a$, let $|a\rangle\langle a|$ act on those listed clock bits and as identity on all other clock bits. Define the five-local propagation term
$$h_\ell=\frac12\left[I_{\rm data}\otimes(|a_\ell\rangle\langle a_\ell|+|b_\ell\rangle\langle b_\ell|)-U_\ell\otimes|b_\ell\rangle\langle a_\ell|-U_\ell^*\otimes|a_\ell\rangle\langle b_\ell|\right],\qquad H_{\rm prop}=\sum_{\ell=1}^Nh_\ell.$$

4. Put $K_0=n+3N$ and $\Delta_0=1/(216(N+1)^3)$, and choose the positive integer
$$J=2K_0+4K_0^2/\Delta_0+1.$$
Output the linearly interpolated Hamiltonian
$$H(s)=(1-s)H_{\rm init}+sH_{\rm final},\quad H_{\rm init}=H_{\rm input}+H_{\rm clock0}+JH_{\rm clock},\quad H_{\rm final}=H_{\rm input}+H_{\rm prop}+JH_{\rm clock}.$$
The term list, integer coefficient $J$, initial preparation, term-access queries, coefficient bits, gate costs, and generator time are explicit coordinates of the path access model ([[def-qa-36-adiabatic-resource-model]]); no spectral projector supplies $A_0$. With $M=n+3N-1$ terms, record the rational certificates $M_1=3N$ for the derivative and $B=M^2J^2$ for every sampled commutator sum; the coefficient functions are the exact constants $1,J$ and affine functions $s,1-s$.

5. Set $\Delta_0=1/[216(N+1)^3]$, $\gamma=3\Delta_0/4$, $B_T=6N/\gamma^2+63N^2/\gamma^3$, and $T=\lceil4B_T/\varepsilon\rceil$. Set the finite-precision simulation tolerance to $\varepsilon_{\rm sim}=\varepsilon/4$. These are finite rational computations.

6. Invoke [[alg-qa-36-discretized-path-simulation]] on the constructed path-access instance with evolution time $T$ and tolerance $\varepsilon_{\rm sim}$. Its output schedule applies the supplied $A_0$ before the path evolution, using each term's declared circuit-family or named-oracle provider. If any required term provider, coefficient evaluation or supported call is unavailable, return no schedule.

7. Declare the data register as the output and the clock register as discarded by the output procedure passed to step 6 (the resulting state is the partial trace over the clock, [[def-qc-partial-trace]]). Record $T$, preparation, simulation calls, coefficient precision, circuit-description and generator costs separately.
proof_obligations: Every h_l is positive semidefinite since its two-pattern block is [I,−U†;−U,I]/2; all other pattern states receive zero from that term. Check endpoint ordering and verify h_l annihilates the selected history. H_clock zero space is exactly monotone unary strings; H_init has a unique all-zero ground vector. Each propagation term acts on at most two computation plus three clock qubits; input terms act on two. Prove the declared polynomial J and complete full-path gap before authoring acceptance; retain all initialization, clock legality and padding assumptions.

items.title: History state and padded output

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: §3.1.1 and Lemma 3.10, PDF pp. 10–15; propagation kernel, input penalty, and padding.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 33, printed pp. 171–176; history-state path and clock trace.

items.statement:
Let the five-local path in [[alg-qa-36-five-local-history-path]] have $N=L+K$ gates, including its $K$ identity gates, and let $V_0=I$ and $V_\ell=U_\ell\cdots U_1$. On the legal unary-clock space, the propagation Hamiltonian has kernel
$$\left\{\frac1{\sqrt{N+1}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{N}V_\ell\xi\otimes|c_\ell\rangle:\xi\in(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\right\}.$$
After adding $H_{\rm input}$, this kernel is one-dimensional and its unit vector is
$$|\eta\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt{N+1}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{N}V_\ell|0^n\rangle\otimes|c_\ell\rangle.$$
The full $H_{\rm final}$ also has this unique ground state. Its data-register marginal is at trace distance at most $L/(N+1)\le\varepsilon/2$ from the specified circuit output state.
proof_obligations: Conjugate H_prop by the controlled prefix-unitary to a path Laplacian tensored with identity; its zero space is uniform clock times arbitrary input. Input energy vanishes exactly for the all-zero input, proving unique selected history ground state. Partial trace gives the average of time-slice density operators; padding bounds the nonfinal weight by ε. Do not infer uniqueness from propagation alone.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite sums, finite-dimensional kernels, and the supplied trace-distance bound.

items.title: Nonnegative monotone ground vector of the history path

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: Claims 3.7–3.8, PDF pp. 13–14; positive and monotone path ground vector for the step-potential path.

references.title: Michael Jarret and Stephen P. Jordan, The Fundamental Gap for a Class of Schrödinger Operators on Path and Hypercube Graphs
references.locator: §§II.2 and III.2, especially Lemma 4; recurrence and ground-vector monotonicity for a linear path potential.

items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$, $a=1-s$, $t=s/2$, and let $L_N$ be the graph Laplacian of the path with vertices $0,1,\ldots,N$. The restriction of the interpolated clock Hamiltonian to legal unary clocks, after removing the data register and propagation unitaries, is
$$H_0(s)=a\,\operatorname{diag}(0,1,\ldots,N)+tL_N.$$
For each $s\in[0,1]$, its smallest eigenvalue is simple and has a normalized nonnegative eigenvector $v(s)=(v_0,\ldots,v_N)$ satisfying
$$v_0\ge v_1\ge\cdots\ge v_N\ge0.$$
For $s>0$ the vector is strictly positive; at $s=0$ it is $e_0$ and its tail coordinates are zero. At $s=1$ it is the uniform vector.
proof_obligations: Prove the finite Perron positivity from an explicit positive power or direct recurrence, then prove monotonicity from the tridiagonal recurrence.
items.axiom_use: None; only finite-dimensional minimization and the stated spectral theorem are used.

items.title: Discretized adiabatic path simulation schedule

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapters 27–30, printed pp. 133–156; discretization and simulation of finite Hamiltonian paths.

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: §§2–3.1, PDF pp. 7–20; finite Hamiltonian descriptions and circuit simulation.

items.statement:
**Input:** An adiabatic path access instance from [[def-qa-36-adiabatic-resource-model]], a nonnegative finite exact time code $T$ from [[def-qa-20-term-list-access-model]], a rational tolerance $0<\varepsilon\le1$, and finite rational certificates $M_1\ge\sup_{s\in[0,1]}\|H'(s)\|$ and $B\ge0$. The time code supports exact comparisons and arithmetic needed to compute $q$ and the derived supported call times. Write $M\ge1$ for the term count. The coefficient functions are real and have the uniform evaluation procedures and error certificates in the access instance. Each requested coefficient approximation is a finitely encoded real rational. The certificate $B$ bounds, for every sampled grid point and its supplied approximations, the commutator sum of the frozen self-adjoint summands. The access record provides supported term-time calls for every product-formula call below, with the requested certified operator errors. If any required coefficient, call, or certificate is unavailable, the algorithm returns no circuit.

**Output:** A finite access schedule that composes the supplied preparation, the segment calls and the declared output procedure, with the requested error budget and separately recorded supplied and generated resources. Each term call uses its declared provider: a supplied circuit-family call or a named-oracle call with its query charge. If all required operations are circuit families, the schedule expands into their composed circuit; otherwise it records each call using its declared provider, including every named-oracle query.

1. If $T=0$, apply the supplied initial preparation $A_0$ and perform the declared output procedure.

2. If $T>0$, set
$$q=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{3TM_1}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil\right\},\qquad \tau=T/q.$$
These are computable finite integers and a supported time code. For each $j=0,\ldots,q-1$, let $s_j=j/q$ and request rational coefficient approximations $\widetilde c_{jk}$ defining $\widetilde H_j=\sum_{k=1}^{M}\widetilde c_{jk}H_k$ with certificate $\|\widetilde H_j-H(s_j)\|\le\varepsilon/(3T)$.

3. Using the input certificate $B$, and supported time codes for all calls below, set
$$r_{\rm PF}=\max\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac{3q\tau^2B}{\varepsilon}\right\rceil\right\}.$$
For each $j=0,\ldots,q-1$ in increasing order, and each product-formula substep $a=1,\ldots,r_{\rm PF}$, execute term calls for $k=M,M-1,\ldots,1$ at time code $(\tau/r_{\rm PF})\widetilde c_{jk}$. This chronological order realizes the algebraic product $S_1(\tau/r_{\rm PF})=e^{-i(\tau/r_{\rm PF})\widetilde c_{j1}H_1}\cdots e^{-i(\tau/r_{\rm PF})\widetilde c_{jM}H_M}$ because circuit products act right to left; $S_1$ is the formula in [[def-qa-20-first-order-product-formula]]. Each of the $qMr_{\rm PF}$ calls is supplied with operator error at most $\varepsilon/(6qMr_{\rm PF})$.

4. Execute the $q$ segment call sequences in increasing $j$ after $A_0$, then perform the declared output procedure. Record initial preparation, term queries, gates, ancillary wires, coefficient bits, circuit-description bits, generator time and $T$ separately. If any required coefficient evaluation, time code or term-exponential access is unavailable, this algorithm has no output schedule under the declared model.
proof_obligations: Duhamel gives piecewise-constant-path error ≤TM₁/(2q)≤ε/6. Coefficient perturbation contributes at most T·ε/(3T)=ε/3; q simulator errors contribute ε/3. Sum all three and reserve remaining ε/6 for A₀/preparation/output implementation if approximate. Every loop has fixed q and finite term count; the term simulator has its explicit positive integer r, including zero commutators.

items.title: Restricted history-path gap

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: Lemma 3.5 and Claims 3.7–3.8, PDF pp. 12–14; path gap through a monotone reversible clock chain.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 33, printed pp. 171–176; legal-clock path spectral gap.

items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ be the number of propagation steps. On the legal-clock block with the zero data input, remove the input penalty and conjugate by the prefix unitaries as in [[lem-qa-36-history-state-ground-and-output]]. The resulting clock matrix is
$$H_0(s)=(1-s)\operatorname{diag}(0,1,\ldots,N)+\frac{s}{2}L_N,$$
where $L_N$ is the path Laplacian. Its ground eigenvalue is simple and its spectral gap is at least $1/(48N^2)$ for every $s\in[0,1]$. In particular, the restricted clock gap is $\Omega(N^{-2})$ uniformly along the path.
proof_obligations: Derive the tridiagonal matrix, prove the small-s disc separation, construct the weighted reversible path chain, bound conductance from monotone stationary weights, and apply the local Cheeger theorem.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite-dimensional variational principles and finite reversible-chain Cheeger inequality only.

items.title: Finite adiabatic path simulation from term access

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: Theorem 1.1 discussion and simulation setup, PDF pp. 3–4.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapters 27–29, printed pp. 133–148; simulation of finite Hamiltonian evolution.

items.statement: Let $H(s)$ be a finite-dimensional Hermitian path with an access instance from [[def-qa-36-adiabatic-resource-model]], a supplied exact preparation isometry $A_0$ of cost $C_{\rm init}$, and finite rational certificates $M_1\ge\sup_s\|H'(s)\|$ and $B$ as required by [[alg-qa-36-discretized-path-simulation]]. Suppose all coefficient evaluations, supported term-time calls, and their certified errors are available. For every nonnegative finite exact time code $T$ supported by the term-list access model and rational $0<\varepsilon\le1$, the algorithm in [[alg-qa-36-discretized-path-simulation]] yields a finite access schedule whose unitary evolution block $\widetilde U_T(1)$ satisfies $\|\widetilde U_T(1)-U_T(1)\|\le\varepsilon$. Before any declared output procedure, its composition with the preparation obeys $\|\widetilde U_T(1)A_0-U_T(1)A_0\|\le\varepsilon$. When all required term operations have full-list uniform circuit-family providers and the resulting circuit generator, including coefficient evaluation and wrapper construction, runs in polynomial time, the schedule expands to a full-list uniform circuit family. If named-oracle providers are used, the schedule records and charges each such query. Its cost record contains $C_{\rm init}$ plus all grid, term-query, gate, ancillary-wire, coefficient-bit, description-bit, and generator-time costs supplied by the access instance.
proof_obligations: Use a Duhamel path-variation estimate and telescope constant-segment simulation errors; state required uniformity and precision.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite-dimensional Duhamel estimates and the declared product-formula simulator only.

items.title: Full-space history-path gap

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Quantum Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: Lemmas 3.11–3.19, PDF pp. 15–20; input-sector decomposition and clock-penalty transfer.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 33, printed pp. 171–176; legal and illegal clock subspaces.

items.statement:
For the path in [[alg-qa-36-five-local-history-path]], put $N=L+K$, $K_0=n+3N$, and
$$\Delta_0=\frac1{216(N+1)^3},\qquad J=2K_0+\frac{4K_0^2}{\Delta_0}+1.$$
For every $s\in[0,1]$, the full Hamiltonian has a unique ground state and its gap is greater than $3\Delta_0/4$. Consequently the minimum gap is $\Omega(N^{-3})$.
proof_obligations: Prove block decomposition, input-energy penalty, legal subspace gap transfer and illegal-clock separation for every s.
items.axiom_use: None; finite-dimensional spectral and block-matrix arguments only.

items.title: Circuit-to-adiabatic simulation

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: Theorem 3.1 and Lemma 3.10, §§3.1.1–3.1.4, PDF pp. 10–20; history path, padding and gap.

references.title: Sabine Jansen, Mary-Beth Ruskai, and Ruedi Seiler, Bounds for the adiabatic approximation with applications to quantum computation
references.locator: Theorem 3 and Lemmas 1–8, PDF pp. 5–12; finite-rank adiabatic bound.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapters 30 and 33, printed pp. 151–156 and 171–176; adiabatic theorem and circuit equivalence.

items.statement:
Let a uniform circuit have $n\ge1$ data qubits and $L\ge1$ gates, each on at most two data qubits. For rational $0<\varepsilon\le1$, set $K=\lceil2L/\varepsilon\rceil$ and $N=L+K$. The construction in [[alg-qa-36-five-local-history-path]] is a five-local finite Hermitian path with a product initial ground state, a unique ground state along the path, gap greater than $3/[864(N+1)^3]$, derivative bound $\|H'\|\le3N$, and $H''=0$. If its term-time providers supply every call required by [[alg-qa-36-discretized-path-simulation]] with the requested certified error at polynomial cost, and coefficient evaluations and output operations also have polynomial cost, the initial ground state can be evolved and the clock discarded to produce a data state at trace distance at most $\varepsilon$ from the circuit output, using
$$T=O(N^{11}/\varepsilon)=O(L^{11}\varepsilon^{-12})$$
continuous evolution time and polynomially many charged term calls, gates, coefficient bits and generator steps. The initial preparation cost, local term access costs, precision costs and output costs are recorded separately by [[def-qa-36-adiabatic-resource-model]].
proof_obligations: Track padding dependence in path length, norm and gap; substitute into JRS with explicit T; add finite Hamiltonian-simulation error and output trace-distance error.
items.axiom_use: None; only the finite-dimensional gap, adiabatic, simulation, and trace-distance results cited below are used.

title: Adiabatic Computation and Circuit Equivalence — Examples

items.title: Two-level avoided crossing

references.title: Sabine Jansen, Mary-Beth Ruskai, and Ruedi Seiler, Bounds for the adiabatic approximation with applications to quantum computation
references.locator: Theorem 3, PDF pp. 5–11; finite gap-dependent bound.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 30, printed pp. 151–156; two-level adiabatic estimates.

items.statement: Consider $H(s)=(s-1/2)Z+X/2$ on $\mathbb C^2$, where $X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Compute its full ground-to-excited gap, derivative bounds, and rank-one JRS error bound.
proof_obligations: Diagonalize and substitute the exact path data.
items.axiom_use: None; a direct $2\times2$ spectral calculation and the cited finite JRS theorem are used.

items.title: Gap closing invalidates a uniform adiabatic bound

references.title: Sabine Jansen, Mary-Beth Ruskai, and Ruedi Seiler, Bounds for the adiabatic approximation with applications to quantum computation
references.locator: Introduction and Theorem 3 hypotheses, PDF pp. 1–5; the gap condition in finite adiabatic estimates.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 30, printed pp. 151–156; gap hypotheses for adiabatic evolution.

items.statement: The $C^2$ path $H(s)=(s-1/2)Z$ has a closing gap and its exact evolution from the initial ground state ends orthogonal to the final ground state. Thus $C^2$ regularity alone does not imply ground-state following or satisfy the uniform-gap hypothesis of the finite JRS theorem.
proof_obligations: Give an explicit 2×2 path and compute the gap and transition probability.
items.axiom_use: None; a direct diagonal evolution calculation is used.

items.title: Two-gate padded history state

references.title: Dorit Aharonov, Wim van Dam, Julia Kempe, Zeph Landau, Seth Lloyd, and Oded Regev, Adiabatic Computation is Equivalent to Standard Quantum Computation
references.locator: §3.1.1, PDF pp. 10–11; propagation terms and history states.

references.title: Andrew M. Childs, Lecture Notes on Quantum Algorithms
references.locator: Chapter 33, printed pp. 171–176; unary-clock history construction.

items.statement:
Take the one-qubit circuit $U_1=X$, $U_2=Z$ and tolerance $\varepsilon=1$. The prescribed padding has $K=4$, $N=6$, and $U_3=\cdots=U_6=I$. Write its legal clocks as $c_0=000000,c_1=100000,\ldots,c_6=111111$. The normalized history state is
$$|\eta\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt7}\bigl(|0\rangle|c_0\rangle+|1\rangle|c_1\rangle-|1\rangle|c_2\rangle-|1\rangle|c_3\rangle-|1\rangle|c_4\rangle-|1\rangle|c_5\rangle-|1\rangle|c_6\rangle\bigr).$$
proof_obligations: Verify each propagation projector annihilates the history state.
items.axiom_use: None; the calculation uses the finite history-state formula and two explicit one-qubit gates.
